reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E, F, and G be finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces equipped with their Borel measurable structures, and let A : E -> G and B : F -> G be continuous real-linear maps. If ||A* t||^2 + ||B* t||^2 = ||t||^2 for every t in G, then the pushforward of the product of the standard Gaussian measures on E and F under (x, y) -> A x + B y is the standard Gaussian measure on G.
objects: Continuous real-linear maps A and B, their inner-product adjoints A* and B*, and standard Gaussian probability measures.
domains: E, F, G: arbitrary finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel spaces; A: E -> G; B: F -> G; t: G; (x,y): E x F.
quantifiers: For every E, F, G and every A, B, the stated condition for every t in G implies the measure identity.
assumptions: For every t in G, ||A* t||^2 + ||B* t||^2 = ||t||^2.
conclusion: The law of A X + B Y is standard Gaussian on G when X and Y are independent standard Gaussian vectors on E and F, respectively.
scopes: The condition ranges over all t in G for the fixed maps A and B; the conclusion is equality of measures on G.
constant_dependencies: No free numerical constants or parameter-dependent bounds; each standard Gaussian has covariance identity on its respective space.
